security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks, code fences, links, or field names and were false positives for Ruby backtick execution, path traversal, and reconnaissance. I confirmed a narrow set of real operational risks: the skill directs users or agents to install and run the RunComfy CLI, authenticate, and submit prompts or media references to RunComfy external API. No prompt injection attempt or covert malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Keep RunComfy commands fixed to the documented model path and require confirmation before npm install, runcomfy login, or runcomfy run.
Clearly state before invocation that prompts, audio URLs, and generation inputs are sent to RunComfy Model API over HTTPS.
Keep the token storage disclosure and advise CI users to prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN without printing tokens or adding them to prompts.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable text-to-video prompts without guessing every RunComfy option. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused Wan 2.7 workflow for prompts, audio URLs, durations, aspect ratios, and outputs.
actual_capabilities: Builds RunComfy Wan 2.7 text-to-video requests from a user prompt.
Documents prompt, audio_url, duration, resolution, aspect_ratio, negative_prompt, prompt expansion, and seed inputs.
Explains when to choose Wan 2.7 instead of HappyHorse, Seedance, Kling, or LTX.
Provides prompt patterns for product showcases, lip-synced spokespeople, and vertical clips.
Describes expected CLI exit codes and troubleshooting references.
limitations: Requires RunComfy CLI, account, and authentication before generation.
Uses RunComfy external API, so prompts and media references leave the local machine.
Wan 2.7 outputs are limited to 15 seconds and 1080p in the documented schema.
Does not create voice in the same pass; lip sync requires a separate audio URL.

use_cases.title: Create Product Motion Ads
use_cases.description: Turn a product brief into a short Wan 2.7 video prompt with camera motion, lighting, resolution, and negative prompts.

use_cases.title: Produce Localized Lip-Sync Clips
use_cases.description: Prepare multiple short clips that use the same visual direction with different approved voiceover audio URLs.

use_cases.title: Select the Right RunComfy Video Model
use_cases.description: Compare Wan 2.7 with related models when a brief needs speed, voice generation, motion editing, or physics-aware motion.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Product Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wan 2.7 on RunComfy to create a five-second 16:9 product video for [product]. Use 1080p and a clear camera move.

prompt_templates.title: Vertical Social Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 9:16 Wan 2.7 prompt for [scene]. Keep one main action, include camera motion, and add concrete negative prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-Synced Spokesperson
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Wan 2.7 RunComfy request for a 12-second lip-synced spokesperson clip using this audio URL: [audio URL]. Match duration, framing, and lighting.

prompt_templates.title: Model Selection Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Wan 2.7, HappyHorse 1.0, Seedance 2.0 Pro, Kling Video O1, and LTX 2 for this video brief: [brief]. Recommend one model and explain the tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Create a premium five-second product video for a new smartwatch.
output: A concise Wan 2.7 generation plan with product framing, lighting, camera movement, 1080p resolution, and 16:9 aspect ratio.
A concrete negative prompt list for avoiding text artifacts, flicker, distorted hands, and unwanted watermarks.

output_examples.input: Make a 12-second vertical lip-sync clip from my approved voiceover URL.
output: A RunComfy-ready direction for a 9:16 spokesperson shot that matches the audio length and visual tone.
Guidance to verify the audio format, duration, and file size before running the generation.

output_examples.input: Which RunComfy video model should I use for fast concept testing?
output_examples.output: A model recommendation that explains whether Wan 2.7, LTX 2, Seedance, Kling, or HappyHorse fits the brief best.

best_practices: Keep each clip focused on one main action, camera move, and subject.
Use audio files that match the documented duration, size, and format limits.
Reuse seeds for close variants and change seeds for broader exploration.
anti_patterns: Submitting long narratives that need multiple scenes in one short clip.
Using vague negative prompts such as bad lighting or bad quality.
Providing audio files outside the supported duration, size, or format range.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code prepare Wan 2.7 text-to-video generations through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Do I need a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires the RunComfy CLI and either an interactive login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Does the video run locally?
faq.answer: No. The local CLI sends the generation request to RunComfy hosted model infrastructure.

faq.question: Can it create lip-synced videos?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a supported WAV or MP3 audio URL that matches the documented duration and size limits.

faq.question: Does Wan 2.7 support 4K output?
faq.answer: No. The documented options are 720p and 1080p.

faq.question: Is my prompt sent outside my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts, audio URLs, and request settings are sent to RunComfy over HTTPS for hosted generation.
